<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via /:name/test (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via /:name/test (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via /:name/test (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /:name/test (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /meta/datasource/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /meta/datasource/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /:name/test (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **8** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3a36dac89f869e9bc72c972dbaf205c3007edbe2` — the merge of head `e8ccebeca528cbacef26dbd96e663f190cf2c59d` into base `8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3a36dac89f869e9bc72c972dbaf205c3007edbe2 && git checkout 3a36dac89f869e9bc72c972dbaf205c3007edbe2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8 e8ccebeca528cbacef26dbd96e663f190cf2c59d && git checkout -B drift-repro 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8 && git merge --no-ff e8ccebeca528cbacef26dbd96e663f190cf2c59d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Read as the net diff of PR #31005 against `main` (merge-base `1aeeafd9d3`) at this head, the PR body, the file list, and the check-runs on `e8ccebeca5` and on the two previous heads `399785c0b1` and `b99ce15091`. The prose faces (`.changeset/datasource-admin-walled-catalog-verdict.md`, `content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`, `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`) were read for ② and ④. Face: the paths decide none and the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line decides the narrowing face, so this tier.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Reused, not restated — right.** `admin-routes.ts` imports `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` from `@objectstack/metadata-core` and asks it once, inside the shared floor `requireDatasourceAdmin`, when a route passes `options.catalogWrite`. No posture test, no rung test and no refusal sentence is written locally; the sentence on the wire is `walled.message`. The four row-writing routes (`POST /datasources`, `PATCH /datasources/:name`, `DELETE /datasources/:name`, `POST /datasources/:name/migrate-credential`) each pass the module-private `DATASOURCE_METADATA_TYPE = 'datasource'`.
- **Asked after the capability gate and before any effect — right.** The floor's order at head: ADR-0069 held-session gate, anonymous refusal, `manage_platform_settings` capability refusal, then the walled verdict, then `return false`. Every handler calls `resolve()` (the service lookup and its `503`) only after the floor returns, and `splitSecret(req.body)` and the service call come after that. So a refused call reaches no `putDatasourceRecord`, `writeSecret`, `removeSecret`, pool registration or re-registration. The §8 matrix pins the service method never called and the store equal to the seed; the PATCH rig pins the stored record and the `sys_secret` ids byte-equal and no pool built.
- **Same status, code and sentence as the `/meta` door — right, with the transport caveat the PR body already names.** The dispatcher's `/meta` save and `_migrate-stored` doors answer `deps.error(walled.message, 403)`, which the status map spells `PERMISSION_DENIED`; this door answers `sendError(res, 403, 'PERMISSION_DENIED', walled.message)`. The REST `/meta` transport spells its 403 `FORBIDDEN`, the grandfathered synonym (ADR-0112 D3 waiver), and this door rightly does not copy it. The type handed to the verdict is `datasource`, the same canonical type `PUT /meta/datasource/:name` hands it, so the subject in the sentence is the same (`a 'datasource' metadata item`); the two edited pins compare the wire message to the verdict's own output for that type and posture rather than to a copied string.
- **Posture source matches `/meta`'s — right.** Both `/meta` transports fold the `tenancy` service through `effectiveTenancyPosture` (`@objectstack/core`). This door, on a host whose kernel has `getServiceAsync`, hands the verdict the admission posture the floor already resolved through `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture`, which folds the same service the same way and raises the branded outage rather than a permit; one read decides both decisions. On a host without that accessor the new `walledVerdictTenancyPosture` reads `ctx.getService('tenancy')` synchronously and folds it with `effectiveTenancyPosture`; a throw reads as `undefined`. That swallow is bounded by the kernel shapes in the tree: `KernelBase`'s `getService` throws only the not-found error and its `registerServiceFactory` is unsupported, while the `is async - use await` throw exists only on `ObjectKernel`, whose plugin context carries `getKernel` with `getServiceAsync`, so the fallback is never reached there. The PATCH rig (no `getKernel`) pins the fallback reading a registered posture and refusing under both walls.
- **Caller rung from the same resolution as `/meta` — right.** `callerPosture` is `authz.posture` off `resolveAuthzContext`; the dispatcher's `ec.posture` is the same field copied by `assemble-execution-context.ts`. `isSystem` is not passed: `ResolvedAuthzContext` carries none and inbound HTTP never does, so the verdict's engine admission is unreachable here, as it was before; the sibling import door passes `authz?.isSystem`, which is the same answer for a wire caller.
- **Operator, `single` and no-tenancy hosts unchanged — right.** The platform operator rung `PLATFORM_ADMIN` derives from the platform anchors (`derivePosture`), never from a held set, so the operator passes the verdict with any key or session that resolves it; §8 pins the operator's key served on all four verbs under `isolated` and `group` with the write landing. The verdict returns allowed for an undefined posture and for `single`; §8b pins all four verbs served for the capability holder under `single` and with no `tenancy` service. §1's write controls moving to the operator's key is the right consequence under `isolated`, and the member's writes under a wall are now §8's subject.
- **The seven non-row routes are unchanged and write nothing — right.** `GET /datasources`, `GET /datasources/drivers`, `GET /datasources/:name`, `POST /datasources/test`, `POST /datasources/:name/test`, `GET /datasources/:name/remote-tables` and `POST /datasources/:name/object-draft` pass no `catalogWrite`. Read in the services: the admin service's store writes (`putDatasourceRecord` at lines 932, 1115, 1326, 1361; `deleteDatasourceRecord` at 1216), `writeSecret`, `removeSecret` and the register/re-register/unregister pool seams are reached only inside `createDatasource`, `updateDatasource` (and its `discardUnstoredSecret`), `removeDatasource` and `migrateCredential`; `testConnection` calls only `config.probe`; `listDatasources` and `getDatasource` read. The external service's `persistObject` and `persistCatalog` are reached only in `importObject` and `refreshCatalog`, which have their own walled door (#30702), never in `listRemoteTables`, `testConnection` or `generateObjectDraft`. §8 pins all seven answering `200` for the member under both walls with the store unchanged.
- **Public surface — none moves.** No exported symbol of `@objectstack/service-datasource` or `@objectstack/metadata-core` changes; the metadata-core edit is two doc-comment door lists; the ADR anchors state the rule the code carries; the datasource docblock's old "no posture arm here" paragraph is replaced because what landed is the imported verdict, not a second local policy.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/service-datasource` **patch** with a **BREAKING** banner and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, the shape 85 other changesets in the tree carry. Right for what the diff publishes: no key of any schema moves, nothing stored changes, no export changes; only the accept set of four routes narrows under a walled posture, which the marker's own words cover.
- `@objectstack/metadata-core` carries no changeset: its diff is doc comments only, so it publishes no behaviour. Right.
- `scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json` gains one row and carries no changeset: it is a repo gate's bookkeeping under a maintainer ruling (#5704, #6664), not a package surface, and the row records a mock, not a consumer. Right.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right. The PR body and the changeset carry the same line and name the same four verbs and the same two postures; the `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: none` lines match the diff (no protocol change; no `skills/**` text teaches these routes).
- The two docs pages state who writes a datasource under a wall and that listing, reading and testing are unchanged, consistent with the code read above.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(1) Ablation head vs this head — the claim holds.** `git diff 56a424acf3 e8ccebeca5 -- packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts` is +5 lines and 0 removed: one paragraph in the `DATASOURCE_ADMIN_CAPABILITY` docblock (blob `c44ff35c97` to `bf51f83b0c`); no code line moved, and no source file of the package moved after `b99ce15091`. The route ablations read at `56a424acf3` therefore transfer. Two seat commits sit on top of `b99ce15091`, both on test files and gate bookkeeping only. `399785c0b1` (+7 lines): module-top side-effect imports of `@objectstack/driver-sql` in both suites and of `@objectstack/driver-memory` in the PATCH rig, the remedy the `check:test-source-alias` gate printed on `b99ce15091` (the suites reach a dynamic driver import inside a clocked case through `sqlite-database-filename.ts`, `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` and `default-datasource-driver-factory.ts`); that gate read OK on `399785c0b1`. `e8ccebeca5` (+16/-1): in the PATCH rig the `@objectstack/driver-memory` warm import is replaced by `vi.mock('@objectstack/driver-memory', …)` whose factory exports an `InMemoryDriver` class that throws on construction, with a three-line comment; and one `otherDeclarations` entry (`kind: mock`, `axis: mock-replacement`, with its `why`) is added to `scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json`, the shape the ledger's existing mock entries take. That answers the one red gate on `399785c0b1` (`check:driver-memory-census`: the warm import was a new `import` binding of that driver with no ledger row; 63 of 64 gates in the lane passed). The ledger file is the gate's own bookkeeping and publishes nothing. Nothing was run here.
- **The mock is sound and changes nothing the suite proves.** Read in the tree: every case in the PATCH rig boots `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` with the suite's own counting `passwordFactory` (`driverFactory` is taken before the `datasource-driver-factory` service lookup, `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` line 396), every datasource it creates is `driver: 'postgres'`, and the suite's store is a hand-rolled map, so the default factory's `memory` arm (`default-datasource-driver-factory.ts` line 1349) and the SQLite fallback's in-memory arm (`sqlite-driver-fallback.ts` line 318), the only two reaches of `@objectstack/driver-memory` in the package, are never called. No case depends on the real in-memory driver, so the mock removes no behaviour from what the pins measure; and because its constructor throws, any future case that did reach that arm would fail loudly rather than pass on a quiet stand-in. The reach the alias gate judges is static, and `main`'s copy of that gate credits a `vi.mock` of the specifier the same as a module-top load.
- **(2) Re-merge — not owed.** The merge-base with `main` is `1aeeafd9d3`; the 14 commits `main` gained since touch no path of this diff (the intersection of the two file lists is empty). The one file in a neighbouring area, `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, is a pin this PR does not read or edit. GitHub reports the PR mergeable with a clean merge; the queue builds the merge commit. One of those 14 commits (`acd190b223`) is the half of `check:test-source-alias` that judges a changed test's reach into the source it loads, and it sits only on `main`: the PR tree carries the older script, so a local run of that gate at the branch tree does not measure the half that went red on `b99ce15091`; the check-run on the merge commit does, and it read OK on `399785c0b1`. The census script is the same on both sides; only the ledger gains a row here. No re-merge is owed for the code; the merge-commit check-runs are the reading that counts.
- **Pre-existing gaps, outside this PR, at rule level.** (a) On a host without an async service lookup the admission's posture read stays unread, as the #15350/#16013 wiring left it; those lines are unchanged here. This PR gives the walled verdict its own read on that host shape, so the walled rule does not inherit the gap; closing the admission's own gap is a change to that wiring with its own pins, not this ruling's. (b) A `tenancy` service that is registered and cannot answer raises the branded outage out of the floor, unchanged by this PR, which adds no throw path. At this door the shipped host's rendering of that throw is pinned `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`admin-routes-authz-outage-envelope.test.ts`); the sibling import door answers the outage inside its guard instead. Whether this floor should answer it inside its guard too, so every host spells it `503`, is a follow-up on the floor, not on this narrowing.
- **Check-runs.** On `b99ce15091` the one red gate was `Test-source alias gate` inside `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`; on `399785c0b1` the one red gate was `driver-memory census gate` in the same lane (63 of 64 gates passed each time; `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI`, `Build Docs`, every other lint and type-check lane, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` and `Spec property liveness` were green on `399785c0b1`). The aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` lanes went red on both from that one gate and from lanes cancelled when the head moved. On `e8ccebeca5`, at the time of this record (47 check-runs): green `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (the lane that carries both gates named above, so the alias gate and the census gate both read OK on this head), `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Build Docs`, `filter`, `Auto Label`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check PR Size`; still pending `Build Core`, `Test Core` (all 8 shards), `Live E2E UI`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`; the UI, temporal and opt-in lanes skipped as before. None red. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record judges the contract, and the queue guard reads them.

### ④ Design judgment

- **A write path at this door that skips the verdict — none found.** Each of the four writing service methods is reached from exactly one route and each of those routes passes `catalogWrite`; no non-row route resolves a writing method (read in ①). The datasource record's other door, `PUT /meta/datasource/:name`, asks the verdict itself. The `migrate_credential` metadata-type action targets this family's route and nothing else.
- **An operator wrongly refused — none found.** The rung is derived from the platform anchors, not from `manage_platform_settings` or a position, and travels on the same resolution as the identity for both a key and a session. Pinned for a key on all four verbs under both walls. An operator whose anchor does not resolve is refused here exactly as at the `/meta` doors: parity, not a regression.
- **A refused PATCH that still mutates secrets or rebuilds a pool — none found.** The refusal precedes `resolve()`, `splitSecret` and the service call; the admin service's secret writes and pool seams all sit inside `updateDatasource`. Pinned byte-equal store and secret ids, no pool built, and the serving pool still answering, under both walls, with the `single` control storing and rebuilding.
- **Posture read on the fallback host.** The swallow-to-`undefined` is bounded by the kernel shapes in the tree (①). A future host shape that both lacks `getServiceAsync` and registers async service factories would read inert there; the docblock states the bound. Not a fix owed on this PR.
- **The in-memory driver mock in the PATCH rig.** Judged in ③: no case in the suite reaches the driver, the mock's constructor throws so a reach would be loud, and the ledger row names it a mock replacement rather than a consumer, which is the disposition the census gate's own words ask for. The two walled PATCH cases still prove what they proved at `b99ce15091`: refusal before the service, byte-equal store and secret ids, no pool built, with the `single` control storing and rebuilding.
- **Rule level.** The PR body and the changeset state the rule, the postures, the verbs, the answer and who moves; neither frames an exploit, names an advisory or narrates a path. The metadata-core comment, the two ADR anchors, the test comments and the ledger row's `why` do the same.
- No must-fix. No should-fix owed on this PR; the two pre-existing items in ③ belong to the floor's own follow-up.
